title: Edge Observability Adapter for Private Clusters with Tenant-Aware Throttling
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Private (VPC/on-prem) customers are deploying Redwood collectors inside their networks. We need an "edge adapter" component that sits in the customer cluster (or VPC subnet) to: 1) enrich and forward traces/metrics/logs to the customer-controlled aggregator or Redwood uplink, 2) enforce tenant-level isolation and throttling, and 3) apply adaptive sampling and quarantine policies for noisy tenants.

Goal: Deliver a lightweight, configurable adapter that can run as a DaemonSet/Deployment in private clusters and provide:
- Tenant-aware ingestion controls (per-tenant rate limits and backpressure signals)
- Distributed tracing hooks to add Redwood context (runtime version, node affinity, model routing hints) to spans without altering application instrumentation
- Adaptive sampling engine configurable by policy (e.g., tail-sampling thresholds, error-rate triggered retention)
- Safe fallback modes when connectivity to Redwood control plane is lost (local buffering, store-and-forward, and quorum-based discard)

Scope: This ticket covers design, prototype implementation, and a smoke-test harness for the adapter. Production hardening (long-term storage, HA across nodes, and k8s operator) will follow in separate tickets.

Out of scope: Full-blown operator, UI for per-tenant policy editing, and encrypted tunnel setup for air-gapped customers (those require additional compliance review).

Constraints & trade-offs:
- We must keep resource usage per-node low (<200MB memory, <5% CPU on 4vCPU nodes) to be viable on customer clusters.
- Enforcing strict per-tenant SLOs at the adapter is best-effort: the adapter signals backpressure to the collector and Redwood ingress but cannot control upstream application rate.
- Sampling decisions at the edge reduce cost and noise but can lose fidelity for debugging high-cardinality incidents; we will add a quarantine mode that increases retention for error spikes.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter binary builds and runs as a k8s DaemonSet with a single configurable YAML
Per-tenant rate limits enforceable via config and visible in adapter logs
Adaptive sampling policy applied: when error-rate > 1% over 1min for a tenant, trace retention increases to 100% for 5 minutes
Span enrichment adds headers: redwood.runtime, redwood.node, redwood-tenant-id without mutating original trace ids
When control-plane unreachable, adapter buffers up to 10,000 spans and forwards after connectivity resumption
Automated smoke tests validate: trace enrichment, throttling, sampling, and buffer drain in CI
tasks: Write ADR for adapter architecture and policy model
Prototype local adapter (Go) with OpenTelemetry receiver + simple policy engine
Integrate adaptive sampling module and unit tests
Add tenant metadata enrichment hook and test span integrity
Create k8s manifest examples: DaemonSet and sidecar pattern
Build smoke-test harness using KinD and synthetic workloads
Open initial PR and request design/PM review
Document rollout and rollback steps for customer installs
comments: 2025-02-14 Asha Patel: Ticket created after R&D spike showed noisy tenants cause >40% of collector CPU in private installs. Initial ask came from Solutions for two enterprise customers.
2025-02-15 Marcus Li: Spike results attached in GH gists (see links). Proposed architecture: keep adapter stateless except for short-lived buffer. Prefer Go binary for low memory profile.
2025-02-16 Evelyn Torres (Design): UX note - policy JSON must be simple and composable. We'll provide examples for 'per-tenant default' and 'tenant-exceptions' patterns.
2025-02-17 Marcus Li: Draft ADR posted - awaiting infra and security review. Key decision: sampling policy lives in adapter and can be overridden by control-plane push or local config when offline.
2025-02-18 Security review (Carlos Mendes): flagged TLS+mutual auth as required for uplink; added requirement to rotate client certs. See link to security checklist.
2025-02-19 Marcus Li: Opened PR #421 on repo 'observability/edge-adapter' with basic OTLP receiver and a stub policy engine. CI smoke tests failing on KinD ingress; investigating port mapping.

2025-02-20 QA (Rina Gupta): Added test plan for chaos scenario: drop uplink for 2m and verify buffer drain and no data corruption. Found edge case with span timestamp ordering—filed follow-up test bug.
2025-02-20 Marcus Li: Marked work 'In Progress' — next is to fix KinD CI and add Prometheus metrics for per-tenant throttled_count and buffer_usage_bytes.
notes_for_rollout: Beta rollout plan: 1) Internal staging (1 cluster) for 2 weeks. 2) Invite 2 pilot customers and run with 'monitor-only' (no throttling) for 1 week. 3) Enable adaptive sampling for pilot tenants and observe metrics for 72 hours. Rollback: reapply manifest with 'adapter.mode=pass-through' which disables sampling and throttling. Communicate changes via release notes and include migration snippet for Helm and raw manifests.
